title: Pediatric Alopecia Triage
subtitle: Common pediatric branches: tinea, AA, traction, trichotillomania, congenital

steps.prompt: Is there scale or inflammation with clinical suspicion for fungal infection?
steps.detail: Broken hairs alone also occur in trichotillomania and alopecia areata. A boggy kerion needs prompt assessment; obtain fungal testing as appropriate without delaying indicated treatment.

steps.prompt: Assess for tinea capitis: fungal testing and clinician-directed systemic treatment when indicated
Are patches smooth and round with exclamation hairs or nail pitting?
Are hairs broken at variable lengths or in reachable/geometric areas?
Is loss marginal or related to tight hairstyles?
Consider congenital, nutritional, endocrine, or biopsy pathway

citations.quote: StatPearls Alopecia review summarizes pediatric alopecia mimickers including tinea capitis, alopecia areata, traction, and traumatic hair loss.
British Association of Dermatologists living guideline includes pediatric and severity-based AA management considerations.
